registered_before: any run of scripts/analysis/lidds_token_cache.py or lidds_token_study.py on LID-DS 2021 or CB-DS; the code is written after this registration and gated on reproducing lidds-ml-v5
owner_decision: 11/11: every design choice of the token model that was made by experiment needs its own evidence (the 39 hooked syscalls one by one, a smallest subset, further syscalls such as getdents, the parameters n, top-10, alpha, folds, trim), the Gumbel threshold must be checked, and the model must be compared with the rule that counts unseen 4-grams, also under a blind attack. LID-DS 2021 may be reused; LID-DS 2019 stays untouched until the owner is told the model is ready for one final run
system_under_study: lidds-ml-v5: token model alone, alphabet select1f, per-thread 4-grams, interpolated Witten-Bell, window score = mean of the 10 highest -ln p, threshold = moment Gumbel on the held-out record maxima of a 5-fold cross-fit without the top 1 %, alpha' = 0.0002 x 0.9, one window fires

data.read: LID-DS 2021 training, validation and the development part of the test recordings (544 attack, 3,403 normal; the split of lidds-evaluation-v3), CB-DS as in cbds-confirmation-v1
data.not_read: the official part of LID-DS 2021, except the declared scorings below; LID-DS 2019
data.cache: one pass per scenario stores, per recording, the distinct (0.5 s window, 6-gram of facts) rows with their counts; a fact is the finest token of the study: (syscall name, errno | open mode + first directory | log2 bucket of a positive return value for the size-capable names | nothing). Every alphabet of the study is a token-wise coarsening of the facts, so its grams and counts follow exactly from the cache

gate: before any result is read: (1) unit test: for select1f the cached path gives the window scores of lidds_ml_token_crossfit.py on the test archive to 1e-9; (2) on the real data the select1f scores equal the stored ml-xfit-tokens scores of every scenario to 1e-9 and the decision reproduces development 530/544 with 6 false-alarm recordings and p95 1.52 s, CB-DS 891/891 with 3. A failed gate stops the study
base_criterion: keeps = development detected >= 530 and false-alarm recordings <= 6 and p95 <= 1.52 s, and CB-DS 891/891 with false-alarm recordings <= 3 (the lidds-ml-v5 development numbers)

q1_hooked_syscalls.units: the 39 syscalls with an exit hook in the probe (sentinel_pulse/ebpf/pulse_token_ids.h); dataset aliases are one unit (pread + pread64, pwrite + pwrite64, recv + recvfrom, send + sendto)
q1_hooked_syscalls.leave_one_out: 39 alphabets: select1f with one unit reduced to its bare name (no errno, no open information, no size); report detected, false-alarm recordings and p95 against the base, pooled and per scenario
q1_hooked_syscalls.smallest_subset: one-pass backward elimination: units ordered by leave-one-out loss of detections (smallest first), then added false alarms, then name; a unit is removed when the alphabet without it and without the units already removed still meets base_criterion; then repeated leave-one-out passes on the remaining set until no unit can be removed. The result S* is a set from which no single unit can be removed, not a proven global minimum
q1_hooked_syscalls.add_one: from select1f: (a) errno for every syscall name of the training recordings that has no exit hook, one name at a time; (b) the size bucket of the return value for getdents, getdents64, readlink, readlinkat, epoll_wait, epoll_pwait, poll, ppoll, select, pselect6, one at a time. A candidate improves when detected >= 533 (three more than the base) with false-alarm recordings <= 6 and CB-DS kept
q1_hooked_syscalls.adoption: select1f stays the alphabet of the system unless the union of the improving candidates, evaluated once on development, also has detected >= 533 with false-alarm recordings <= 6 and CB-DS kept. Then the union is scored once on official (declared reuse) and adopted only with detected > 1238 and false-alarm recordings <= 26; adoption needs a new probe build, capture and live run. S* is scored once on official as a declared reuse and reported next to select1f; it is not adopted here (it changes the probe, and the overhead it saves is not measured by this protocol)

q2_parameters.report: development detected, false-alarm recordings, p95 and CB-DS for every grid point; the base is (4, 10, 0.00018, 5, 0.01)
q2_parameters.decision: none: report only. The parameters were chosen on development with attack labels before; this grid states how sensitive the result is, it does not select again

checks: calibration out of sample: for each alpha' of the grid, the number of development normal test recordings whose maximum exceeds the threshold, against the expected number alpha' x recordings, with a Clopper-Pearson interval, pooled and per scenario

goodness of fit of the held-out maxima per scenario: Anderson-Darling statistic for the moment Gumbel with a parametric-bootstrap p-value (2,000 draws), and the maximum-likelihood GEV shape with a profile 95 % interval
the same threshold written as mean + k x standard deviation of the trimmed maxima: k as a function of alpha'

label-free alternatives at the same realised false-alarm budget (false-alarm recordings <= 3, 6, 12, 20, 34 on development): Gumbel by maximum likelihood, GEV by maximum likelihood, normal, the largest held-out maximum, the split-conformal order statistic
q3_gumbel.decision: none for the system. 'Gumbel holds' is claimed only if the pooled observed count lies inside the 95 % interval at every alpha' and fewer than 2 of 15 scenarios reject at 5 % after Holm; otherwise the thesis states that alpha' is a tuning knob and reports the measured ratio. An alternative that detects more at every budget is recorded as a candidate for a later protocol

q4_model_or_novelty_rule.rule: window score = number of events whose full 4-gram was never seen in the learning recordings (same cross-fit, same trimmed moment Gumbel, same one-window decision); second rule: events with an unseen 4-gram or an unseen token
q4_model_or_novelty_rule.matched_comparison: development recall of model and rules at false-alarm budgets <= 3, 6, 12, 20, 34 recordings (alpha' swept per method); difference model minus rule at the budget of 6 with a paired bootstrap over recordings stratified by scenario (10,000 draws)
q4_model_or_novelty_rule.blind_attack_simulation: seen-only attack: from every development attack recording, every row whose 4-gram or last token is unseen by the final model is removed, as if the attacker had avoided every unseen sequence; the model is scored on what is left with the registered threshold. The unseen-gram rule scores 0 on these by construction. Reported: detected recordings, per scenario, and which seen grams carry the detections. The same stripping is applied to development normal recordings as a control. It is a semi-synthetic lower bound: removing events is not a real exploit, and the following grams are not rebuilt
q4_model_or_novelty_rule.decision: none for the system: the model stays (owner: ML first). The thesis states which of the two has an advantage where, by these numbers

official_scorings_declared: at most two, each once and written with write_once: S* of q1, and the union of q1 if it qualifies. No other official score is computed
multiple_comparisons: q1 looks at about 150 alphabets on development with attack labels, so single differences of one or two recordings are noise; the thresholds of 3 recordings and the single official confirmation are the guard, and per-unit leave-one-out differences are reported with the count only
limits: development has been looked at many times; every number of this study is development unless marked official
the dataset order is the exit order of sysdig; the probe emits unhooked syscalls at entry (probe1f gave the same development result as select1f)
the size bucket of non-I/O return values (poll, epoll_wait) is the number of ready descriptors, not bytes
CB-DS has no exploit times: detection is any alarm
